description: standards/058-notifications.md NF2 and NF11: the messages the pipeline speaks, all of them 055 AM1 envelopes. notification.requested is internal, produced by notify.decide through the outbox (AM4) and consumed by notify.send.<channel>. The four status events are what a provider's webhook becomes after 055 AM8 re-envelopes it: source is /<adapter name>, id is the provider's own event id, subject is the notification_id the adapter resolved from the provider's message id, and data is the shape below. The record's status moves only along the transitions listed; an event that arrives for a transition not listed is recorded in the inbox and ignored, because providers redeliver and reorder.

notification.requested.subject: notification_id
notification.requested.produced_by: notify.decide, in the transaction that wrote the record (055 AM4); notification.release, for a deferred record whose not_before has passed

data.description: Only the reference. The send job reads the record, resolves the address, renders, and sends; the payload travels in the row, never twice.

notification.requested.record_status_on_consume: sent (provider accepted) | failed (permanent refusal, retries exhausted) | unknown (at_most_once crash between the provider call and the record)

notification.bounced.subject: notification_id

kind.description: NF7. hard suppresses the address for every class; soft is retried under 055 AM5 and suppresses nothing.

detail.description: The provider's diagnostic, for an operator. Never rendered to the recipient.

notification.bounced.side_effects: kind = hard: the identity's channel address gains suppression { reason: hard_bounce }; a transactional bounce is an alert (NF3)

notification.complained.subject: notification_id
notification.complained.side_effects: the identity's channel address gains suppression { reason: complaint }: optional notifications stop, transactional continue (NF7)

notification.failed.subject: notification_id
notification.failed.side_effects: a transactional failure is an alert (NF3)

transitions_note: deferred -> suppressed happens when notification.release finds the address suppressed or the preference withdrawn since notify.decide ran: consent is re-checked at release. unknown -> sent|failed is notification.reconcile's, the at_most_once reconciler named in notify.send's declaration (057 JB4). bounced, complained, failed, suppressed and collapsed are terminal; a later delivered for a bounced row is a provider reorder and is ignored.
